deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the reverse (closing part) of a faint letter in German Kurrent. It is signed (most plausibly) 'K. Hattendorff', the Göttingen mathematician Karl Hattendorff, who edited Riemann's posthumous memoir on minimal surfaces, 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867/68), and who prepared it for Riemann's Werke (1876). The legible fragments concern editorial and priority matters around minimal surfaces:
(1) a wish that reference be made to Herr Schwarz and to Herr Schondorff. Schondorff wrote the Göttingen prize essay on minimal surfaces, and the letter mentions 'seiner Preisschrift' (his prize essay).
(2) a mention of the relation of Schwarz's work to Weierstraß. 'Weierstraß' stands out legibly on line 6.
(3) an enclosure of Schondorff's Abhandlung, which 'will surely please you'.
(4) a request concerning the judgment of the Göttingen faculty/Academy (the prize jury) and the great significance of something Gaussian, perhaps 'der Gaußischen Bedeutung'.
(5) leaving it to the addressee's decision whether a short or a somewhat longer introduction ('Einleitung') should accompany the printing ('Abdruck').
(6) an offer to enclose a manuscript by Riemann on something involving a 'Kugel' (sphere), which Hattendorff had received from Dedekind.
(7) closing formulas: 'Hochachtung', 'Ihr ergebenster', signature.
The surrounding pages fit this reading. The next page is a letter dated Göttingen, 18 January 1876, almost certainly from H. A. Schwarz (in Göttingen from 1875) to Heinrich Weber (then in Königsberg, 'K.'), the editor of Riemann's Werke. In it Schwarz complains about Hattendorff's carelessness in the minimal-surface section of the proofs. So the folio belongs to the editorial correspondence around the minimal-surface paper, not to Riemann's own mathematical notes. There is no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Editorial correspondence (Hattendorff) about publishing Riemann's minimal-surface memoir: references to Schwarz, Schondorff's prize essay, Weierstraß, an introduction to the printing, and a Riemann manuscript received from Dedekind
results.modern_name: Historical/editorial context of the Plateau problem papers (Riemann 1867, Weierstraß 1866, Schwarz 1865-67, Schondorff 1868)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is not by Riemann and contains no mathematics. It is part of a letter by Hattendorff about the editing and publication of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir. Its historical interest is limited to editorial and priority context (Schwarz, Schondorff, Weierstraß, Dedekind), and that context is broadly known from the history of Riemann's Werke.
transcription_corrections: The page is extremely faint; most words in the machine transcription are guesses and should stay marked uncertain.
Line 6 clearly reads 'Weierstraß' (written larger and darker than the rest).
'Schondorff' recurs (lines 3 and 7: 'Schondorff's Abhandlung'); it is consistent with the author of the Göttingen prize essay on minimal surfaces.
The signature at the bottom right appears to be 'K. Hattendorff' (initial uncertain), preceded by 'Ihr ergebenster'.
'der Gaußischen Bedeutung' is uncertain; it may be a different noun following 'Gaußischen'.
The line 'von Riemann über das ... Kugel' is uncertain; 'Kugel' is a plausible but unconfirmed reading.
